record.original_question: Determine whether the incompressible Euler equations are ill-posed in the Besov spaces B^1_{infinity,q} for 1 < q < infinity.

evidence.quote: Problem 7. Are the Euler equations (1.1) ill-posed in the Besov spaces B∞,q for 1 < q < ∞? To put this problem in a functional space context, first recall that H s ⊂ C 1+α ⊂ B∞,1 1 ⊂ C 1 ⊂ Lip ⊂ F∞,2 1 1 ⊂ B∞,∞ ⊂ logLip ⊂ C β 1 for any 0 < α, β < 1 and s > n/2 + 1 + α and next observe that, in the specified range, the B∞,q 1 1 spaces interpolate between B∞,1 and the Zygmund space B∞,∞ .

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the incompressible Euler equations on $\mathbb{R}^n$ (with $n \ge 2$):
$$\partial_t u + (u\cdot\nabla)u + \nabla p = 0, \qquad \nabla\cdot u = 0, \qquad u(0,\cdot)=u_0,$$
for the velocity field $u:[0,T)\times\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n$ and pressure $p$.

For $s\in\mathbb{R}$ and $1\le q\le\infty$, the inhomogeneous Besov space $B^{s}_{\infty,q}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ is defined via a Littlewood–Paley decomposition $(\Delta_j)_{j\ge -1}$ as the space of tempered distributions $f$ with finite norm
$$\|f\|_{B^{s}_{\infty,q}} = \Big\| \big(2^{js}\|\Delta_j f\|_{L^\infty}\big)_{j\ge -1}\Big\|_{\ell^q}.$$
It is known that $B^{1}_{\infty,1}$ embeds into $C^1$, which embeds into the Lipschitz class, which embeds into the Zygmund class $B^{1}_{\infty,\infty}$; and for $1<q<\infty$ the spaces $B^{1}_{\infty,q}$ interpolate between $B^{1}_{\infty,1}$ and $B^{1}_{\infty,\infty}$. Local ill-posedness of the Euler equations is already established in the endpoint critical spaces $C^1$, $B^{1}_{\infty,1}$, and $B^{1}_{\infty,\infty}$.

Determine, for each $q$ with $1<q<\infty$, whether the Cauchy problem for the incompressible Euler equations is locally ill-posed in $B^{1}_{\infty,q}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ (e.g. in the sense of failure of continuous dependence of the solution map on the initial data, or instantaneous norm inflation).
artifact.category_tag: Ill-posedness of incompressible Euler equations in critical Besov spaces
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work has established ill-posedness for the incompressible Euler equations in the endpoint critical Besov spaces $B^{1}_{\infty,1}$ (Bourgain–Li, and subsequent refinements) and in $B^{s}_{p,\infty}$ spaces (with third index $\infty$, including the Zygmund-type endpoint). However, the intermediate critical scale $B^{1}_{\infty,q}$ for $1<q<\infty$ does not appear to be settled by the recovered literature; results explicitly target $q=1$ or $q=\infty$ rather than the open interval, so the problem appears to still be open.

status_evidence.title: Ill-posedness for the Euler equations in Besov spaces
status_evidence.snippet: construct an initial data u_0 in B^sigma_{p,infty} and show the solution map is discontinuous at t=0
status_evidence.claim: Ill-posedness is established with the third Besov index equal to infinity, not for 1<q<infinity.

status_evidence.title: Local ill-posedness of the incompressible Euler equations in C^1 and B^1_{infty,1}
status_evidence.snippet: Local ill-posedness of the incompressible Euler equations in C^1 and B^1_{infty,1}
status_evidence.claim: Endpoint case q=1 of the scale B^1_{infty,q} is known to be ill-posed.

status_evidence.title: Ill-posedness in B^s_{p,infty} of the Euler equations: Non-continuous dependence
status_evidence.claim: Recent ill-posedness results focus on the q=infinity endpoint case.
